answer: Sybil resistance requires more than MRENCLAVE, which identifies enclave code, not a unique machine: each identity must also bind to an enclave-held key and a verifier-checked hardware attestation, with issuance limited to one identity per silicon device. Under that policy, copying a virtual machine cannot reproduce the trusted key or obtain another valid identity; scaling identities requires additional physical hardware, not merely storage as cheap as timber or bandwidth across an ocean, even at the nadir of hardware prices.
